source.book: 《史记》卷一百二十六《滑稽列传》
source.excerpt: 優孟，故楚之樂人也。長八尺，多辯，常以談笑諷諫。楚莊王之時，有所愛馬，衣以文繡，置之華屋之下，席以露床，啗以棗脯。馬病肥死，使群臣喪之，欲以棺槨大夫禮葬之。左右爭之，以為不可。王下令曰：「有敢以馬諫者，罪至死。」優孟聞之，入殿門。仰天大哭。王驚而問其故。優孟曰：「馬者王之所愛也，以楚國堂堂之大，何求不得，而以大夫禮葬之，薄，請以人君禮葬之。」王曰：「何如？」對曰：「臣請以彫玉為棺，文梓為槨，楩楓豫章為題湊，發甲卒為穿壙，老弱負土，齊趙陪位於前，韓魏翼衛其后，廟食太牢，奉以萬戶之邑。諸侯聞之，皆知大王賤人而貴馬也。」王曰：「寡人之過一至此乎！為之柰何？」優孟曰：「請為大王六畜葬之。以壟灶為槨，銅歷為棺，齎以薑棗，薦以木蘭，祭以糧稻，衣以火光，葬之於人腹腸。」於是王乃使以馬屬太官，無令天下久聞也。
source.transcriptionNote: 复用现有已录入批次的逐字原文快照；底本定位、原件哈希及行号保留。电子本尚不宣称纸本异文全校。

panels.title: 被宠爱的马
panels.caption: 楚庄王十分宠爱自己的马，让它住在华美的屋里。
panels.scene: Recollection: chestnut horse with white blaze stands in ornate ancient stable with embroidered cloth; cinnabar-robed king admires it.

evidence.excerpt: 有所愛馬，衣以文繡，置之華屋之下

panels.title: 要厚葬爱马
panels.caption: 马死后，楚庄王打算按大夫的礼仪，把它厚葬。
panels.scene: King looks sorrowfully toward motionless chestnut horse resting peacefully on a mat in stable; no gore, no funeral has happened.

panels.title: 不许再劝
panels.caption: 群臣劝说不妥，楚庄王却不许他们再提。
panels.scene: Ancient hall: worried courtiers bow in remonstrance, king raises a firm hand to stop them.

panels.title: 优孟大哭
panels.caption: 优孟走进殿门，仰头大哭，把楚庄王都惊住了。
panels.scene: Tall teal-robed You Meng enters hall dramatically lamenting with head raised; king looks surprised.

panels.title: 规格还不够高
panels.caption: 他反而说：“这么受宠的马，只按大夫礼葬，太薄了！应该用国君的礼。”
panels.scene: You Meng proposes an even grander idea with sweeping respectful gesture, king listens curiously. No actual funeral.

panels.title: 越说越夸张
panels.caption: 优孟一口气说起玉棺、珍木、劳师动众的葬礼。
panels.scene: You Meng counts extravagant imaginary requirements on his fingers; small jade block and wooden sample sit on table as visual metaphors, no grand funeral physically occurring.

panels.title: 一句点醒楚王
panels.caption: “诸侯听说了，就都知道您把人看得轻，把马看得重了。”楚庄王终于承认自己错了。
panels.scene: Close view: You Meng expression turns earnest, king lowers gaze in realization, courtiers quietly attentive.

evidence.excerpt: 皆知大王賤人而貴馬也

panels.title: 不再厚葬
panels.caption: 楚庄王把马交给掌管膳食的官署处理，不再照原计划厚葬。
panels.scene: Final hall scene: king calmly withdraws elaborate funeral plan, gestures to a plain-robed official; You Meng bows. No cooking, no butchery, no actual lavish coffin.

evidence.excerpt: 於是王乃使以馬屬太官

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: a finished Histree vintage Chinese lianhuanhua story atlas, exactly 8 sequential illustrations on ONE image. Primary request: 优孟劝止厚葬马. Composition: STRICT equal rectangular grid of TWO columns and 4 rows. Read left to right, top to bottom. All row heights equal, all column widths equal. Canvas target 1024 x 1280. Narrow straight cream gutters, maximum 4 pixels; no outer margin, no header/footer; every scene fills its own complete LANDSCAPE cell. No merged panels, insets, or changes in layout.
Style: classic 1950s-1960s Chinese small-picture storybook, early Shanghai Animation folk-art sensibility. Graceful expressive fine ink outlines, hand-painted gouache, mineral blue/green, muted cinnabar and ochre, textured warm cream paper, restrained humor and human facial expressions. Rich but legible environments; varied wide/medium/close shots. NOT modern anime, 3D, glossy or photorealistic. Ancient China, no modern objects. No words, letters, numbers, captions, speech balloons, calligraphy, watermark or symbols that look like writing ANYWHERE. Clothing and face continuity within the atlas is essential.
Characters and invariants: You Meng: tall adult court entertainer in teal robe with ochre sash, expressive long face, neat moustache, simple black cap. King Zhuang of Chu: mature king in cinnabar robe and dark Chu crown, black beard. Beloved horse: chestnut with white blaze, only shown standing in recollection or resting motionless with eyes closed, no gore. NO actual lavish funeral or cooked horse: imagined funeral props remain small objects on table or gestural explanation, not real events. No cruelty shown.
Scenes in this exact order:
1. Recollection: chestnut horse with white blaze stands in ornate ancient stable with embroidered cloth; cinnabar-robed king admires it.
2. King looks sorrowfully toward motionless chestnut horse resting peacefully on a mat in stable; no gore, no funeral has happened.
3. Ancient hall: worried courtiers bow in remonstrance, king raises a firm hand to stop them.

6. You Meng counts extravagant imaginary requirements on his fingers; small jade block and wooden sample sit on table as visual metaphors, no grand funeral physically occurring.
7. Close view: You Meng expression turns earnest, king lowers gaze in realization, courtiers quietly attentive.
8. Final hall scene: king calmly withdraws elaborate funeral plan, gestures to a plain-robed official; You Meng bows. No cooking, no butchery, no actual lavish coffin.

styleRefinement.instructions: Use case: style-transfer. Restyle ONLY IMAGE 1, the edit target. IMAGE 2 (approved older 移木立信 artwork) is the PRIMARY style reference; IMAGE 3 (newly corrected fish-refusal artwork) is a SECONDARY reference for the same approved style. Do not import reference story events, characters, sword/pole/fish props, captions or text. Draw the target in the same artistic language as images 2 and 3: strongly designed Chinese folk/early Shanghai animation characters, larger expressive heads, compact stylized adult bodies, angular expressive eyebrows and noses made with very few confident strokes, small curved eyes, humorous expressive poses, fluid varied BLACK ink contours, FLAT matte pigment blocks with only spare broad ink-wash texture. Reduce realistic anatomy, skin modeling, facial shading, brocade patterns, tiny clothing folds and detailed background rendering dramatically. Robes are mostly solid muted color fields with spare trim, NO all-over elaborate embroidery. Simplify background buildings into rhythmic geometric silhouettes, light ink washes and warm UNPAINTED cream space. Restrained indigo, ochre and cinnabar, subtle paper grain like image 2, no dense brown texture overlay. NOT realistic illustrated portraiture, glossy painting, modern anime, chibi toys, 3D or photorealism. Keep all characters ADULT unless explicitly elderly. Preserve each character's consistent identifying robe color, beard and role, but redraw their form in this stylized way. No words, numerals, letters, title, captions, calligraphy, speech bubbles, watermark or readable marks ANYWHERE, including on documents, garments or props. Ignore all text visible in the style reference. Do not add a header or footer.

previousAfterword.title: 越赞成，越显出不妥
paragraphs: 《史记·滑稽列传》记优孟没有正面重复群臣的劝告，而是把厚葬的规格继续往上推，借此让楚庄王看清轻重颠倒。
优孟列举的盛大葬礼只是劝说内容。结尾依原文保留交太官处理，不画杀马、烹煮等场面。

takeaway.title: 关爱也要分清轻重
takeaway.text: 在自己的喜爱之外，还要看看决定会怎样影响别人。
